nodes.text: Confounded attribution: correct belief via unreliable process fails when cost opposes evidence.

evidence.text: Confounded attribution: evidence and cost usually move together; a society opening removes punishment and stress-tests old reasons, so one can land on the correct anchor for the wrong reason. A correct belief via unreliable process fails when cost and evidence next oppose.

nodes.text: Misperceived reference corrupts everything downstream with no layer flawed.

evidence.text: Misperceived reference: thinking a norm still forbids what it allows, or a market is risk-off when it turned. Error upstream of anchor, responsiveness, and policy; corrupts every downstream judgment with none of the three flawed.

nodes.text: Reference lag: diaspora freezes the origin norm at emigration; Quebec keeps dropped features.

evidence.text: Reference lag: apparent principle is conformity to a stale clock. Diaspora communities preserve older language forms; Quebec French keeps features metropolitan French dropped. The real reference is the origin norm frozen at emigration day.

nodes.text: Prior prediction under the old regime, with reasons, is the trustworthy test.

evidence.text: The prior prediction test: what was predicted, before the change, with reasons attached. 'I'll understand incentives better by 40' is falsifiable; 'more to protect' is incentives wearing insight; 'I'd wear this if society let me' tests the anchor. With no prior prediction the case is underdetermined; never default to the flattering interpretation.

nodes.text: Behavioral consistency was a bad proxy; the trusted question is asked in advance.

evidence.text: Verdict: consistency of behavior was never the admired thing, only a bad proxy for process (anchor, responsiveness, evidence vs cost). Stories afterward are mostly unfalsifiable; the only trusted question is asked in advance: what will you do when it changes, and why?
